_meta.indication: MYOZYME (alglucosidase alfa) is indicated for use in patients with Pompe disease (GAA deficiency); it has been shown to improve ventilator-free survival in patients with infantile-onset Pompe disease compared to an untreated historical control, whereas use in other forms of Pompe disease has not been adequately studied to assure safety and efficacy

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study AGLU01602 (AGLU-1602), the severe infantile-onset study
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.phase: Dose-ranging study; the application was granted priority review as a new molecular entity (no formal phase labeled in review)
pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, randomized, open-label, dose-ranging study of Myozyme IV 20 mg/kg vs 40 mg/kg every other week for at least 52 weeks; an untreated Historical Control Subgroup was used in lieu of a concurrent placebo control
pivotal_trials.population: Infantile-onset Pompe disease, defined as GAA deficiency with clinical signs of disease by age six months and cardiac hypertrophy; patients with respiratory insufficiency or prior enzyme therapy were excluded
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was invasive ventilator-free survival, analyzed as the pooled Kaplan-Meier estimate of survival to 18 months
pivotal_trials.n: 19 patients enrolled; 1 excluded for ventilation at baseline, leaving 18 patients randomized equally to 20 mg/kg and 40 mg/kg
pivotal_trials.result: Estimated proportion alive and ventilator-free at 18 months was 83% (95% CI 59% to 96%), substantially higher than the 1.6% 18-month survival rate in the untreated Historical Control Subgroup

nct_ctgov.title: A Study of the Safety and Efficacy of rhGAA in Patients With Infantile-onset Pompe Disease

key_safety: Most serious adverse reactions were cardiorespiratory failure and anaphylactic reactions; life-threatening anaphylactic reactions including anaphylactic shock occurred during infusion. Infusion reactions occurred in 20 of 39 (51%) of patients in clinical studies. The most common adverse events included pyrexia/fever (36 of 39, 92%), cough (18 of 39, 46%), rash (21 of 39, 54%), vomiting (19 of 39, 49%), diarrhea (24 of 39, 62%), and pneumonia (18 of 39, 46%)
target_moa: Alglucosidase alfa is a recombinant form of the human lysosomal enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) that provides an exogenous source of GAA; it is taken up into cells and transported to lysosomes where it degrades glycogen by hydrolyzing alpha-1,4- and alpha-1,6-glycosidic linkages, addressing the GAA deficiency causing Pompe disease
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase produced in a Chinese hamster ovary cell line) used for enzyme replacement therapy

boxed_warning.content: Life-threatening anaphylactic reactions, including anaphylactic shock, have been observed in patients during MYOZYME infusion; because of the potential for severe infusion reactions, appropriate medical support measures should be readily available when MYOZYME is administered

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened to discuss this application; it was instead discussed at a CDER Regulatory Briefing on March 3, 2006

summary.text: Myozyme received Orphan Designation (1997) for glycogen storage disease type II, Fast Track Designation (2003) for preventing mortality in classical infantile Pompe disease, and Priority review; it was approved as a new molecular entity based on improved ventilator-free survival in infantile-onset Pompe disease versus an untreated historical control, without an advisory committee meeting or accelerated approval

requirement.text: Complete the juvenile- and adult-onset (late-onset) Pompe disease study AGLU02704, a randomized, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled study of safety, efficacy and pharmacokinetics of Myozyme in late-onset Pompe disease

citations.quote: Genzyme commits to completing the juvenile- and adult-onset Pompe disease study AGLU02704, entitled "A randomized, double-blind, multicenter, multinational, placebo-controlled study of the safety, efficacy and pharmacokinetics of Myozyme, recombinant human acid alpha-glucosidase (rhGAA), treatment in patients with late-onset Pompe disease." Patient accrual is complete, the study is to be completed by September 30, 2007, and a final study report will be submitted to CDER by May 31, 2008.

requirement.text: Design and implement an infantile-onset Pompe disease study to assess growth and development with alglucosidase alfa treatment in patients less than one year of age at study entry, with blinded assessments over a 10-year period

citations.quote: 5. Genzyme commits to designing and implementing an infantile-onset Pompe disease study to assess growth and development with treatment with alglucosidase alfa, in patients who are less than one year of age at study entry. This study is to include blinded assessments of growth (including standardized measurements of recumbent length, height, weight, and head circumference), developmental testing (the scales used need to be prospectively agreed upon), auditory and visual screening, neuro-imaging, and antibody assessments at 6- to 12-month intervals over a 10-year period. A study protocol will be submitted to CDER by September 29, 2006, for concurrence, and the study will be initiated by January 31, 2007. The final study report for this study will be submitted to CDER by September 30, 2017.

requirement.text: Design and implement immune tolerance protocols in Pompe disease patients with significant/neutralizing antibody titers who are failing treatment, and a preventive immune tolerance protocol for patients at high risk

citations.quote: 6. Genzyme commits to designing and implementing an immune tolerance protocol in Pompe disease patients who have significant antibody titers, or the presence of neutralizing antibody, and are failing treatment. Genzyme commits to designing and implementing a preventive immune tolerance protocol in Pompe disease patients at high risk for the development of significant immune responses to the product. This would involve 1) establishing the correlation among genotype, the level of \alpha-glucosidase protein (non-enzymatic assay), and the presence and levels of binding, \text{IgE}, and neutralizing antibodies over time, using validated assays; and 2) developing an immune tolerance regimen that would be implemented before or concomitant with onset of therapy for those at high risk. Additionally, Genzyme commits to monitoring antibody positive patients, whose immune responses are not associated with loss of efficacy or severe hypersensitivity responses, at regular intervals over an extended period of time (i.e., 18-24 months) to specifically assess if a sub-population of patients become tolerant with routine treatment. Reports from preclinical studies to assess potential tolerance regimens and a commitment for timelines for a subsequent clinical study will be submitted to CDER by December 29, 2006.

requirement.text: Design and implement a dose- and dose-interval exploration study in patients with poor responses to treatment regardless of antibody status, including infantile-, juvenile-, and adult-onset populations

citations.quote: 7. Genzyme commits to designing and implementing a dose- and dose-interval exploration study in patients with poor responses to treatment, regardless of antibody status. This study is to include patients in the infantile-, juvenile-, and adult-onset patient populations. A study protocol will be submitted to CDER by September 29, 2006, for concurrence, and the study will be initiated by January 31, 2007. The final study report for this study will be submitted to CDER by September 30, 2009.
